# User guide: Workspaces

## In plain words

A workspace is one agent working in one folder, with one terminal, under one name. You start a workspace with the **New Workspace** button and its folder picker. Every open workspace has a row in the drawer, the list that slides out at the left side of the page. The workspace keeps running on the server when you close the browser tab. You can open it again from another browser or from your phone. When you close a workspace, the plugin saves its place, and you can resume the same conversation later. This page explains the picker, the drawer, the menu of each row, and what is kept when you close or restart a workspace.

## Where to find it

- **The AI CLI Agents tab** in the Unraid top menu. See [Getting started](getting-started.md).
- **The drawer.** It slides out from the left edge of the page. Press the tab at the left edge, which shows a "bars" icon when the drawer is closed, to open it. Press the same tab (it then shows an arrow) to close it. A click outside the drawer, or the Escape key, also closes it, unless the drawer is pinned.
- **New Workspace.** The button at the top of the drawer. It opens the picker, a window called **Select Workspace**.
- **Select Workspace.** The same picker opens from this button when you have no workspace open. The page then shows **No Active Workspaces**.
- **The row menu.** Each row has a three-dot icon. Select it to open the menu of that workspace. A right-click on a row opens the same menu. On a keyboard, use the context-menu key or Shift plus F10.

This page does not cover the settings of one workspace (launch arguments, environment variables, secrets), favourites, export and import, or automatic continue. Those are in [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md).

## How to use it

### Start a workspace

1. Open the drawer and press **New Workspace**.
2. Expect: the window **Select Workspace** opens. It has up to three sections: **Favourites**, **Agent** and **Folder**.
3. In **Agent**, select a tile. Each tile shows the icon and the name of an installed agent. The tile you select gets a tick. The picker remembers your last choice in this browser.
4. In **Folder**, choose the folder. See the next part.
5. Look at the bar above the footer. It reads **Will start**, the agent, and the last three folders of the path. This is exactly what the buttons will do.
6. Press **Start New**, or **Resume** if it is there. See "Resume or Start New".
7. Expect: the window closes. A row for the workspace appears in the drawer and becomes the active workspace. The page shows "Starting" and the name of the agent. The terminal opens.

The row gets the name of the folder (the name **Root** for the folder `/`). You can rename it later.

You can have several workspaces open at once. You can also open two workspaces for the same agent and the same folder. For example, you can run a review in a second workspace while the first one keeps working.

If you press **Cancel**, the close button (the cross at the top right) or the Escape key, the window closes and nothing starts. Escape does not close the window while a smaller dialog is open on top of it. Close the smaller dialog first.

### Choose the folder

The **Folder** section is one panel. It holds a path bar, a filter row, the list of folders and a field for a new folder.

- **Where the picker starts.** It starts in the folder of the active workspace. If you have none, it starts in the folder of the workspace you closed last on this page. If there is none, it starts in **Starting folder** (`/mnt/user` by default). If a folder cannot be read, the picker goes back to `/mnt`.
- **The path bar.** Each part of the path is a button. Select a part to jump to that folder in one click. The current folder is the last part, and it is not a button.
- **Select a folder.** Click a folder once to select it. The row gets an orange bar and the tag **Selected**. Press Space on a row for the same result.
- **Open a folder.** Double-click a folder to go into it. Press Enter on a row for the same result. **Up one level** is always the first row of a subfolder.
- **Folder outside `/mnt`.** A path that does not start with `/mnt/` makes the picker frame and the drawer row glow red. Your array, your pools and your disks are all under `/mnt`.
- **The target.** A workspace starts in the selected folder. If you selected none, it starts in the folder that the path bar shows.
- **New folder.** Type a name in the field **New Folder...** and press **Create**. The picker goes into the folder that it created, so the next press of **Start New** starts the workspace there. If a name is typed before the first list loads, the picker keeps it. The picker clears the name when you go to another folder.
- **Show more folders.** The list shows 100 folders at a time. Press **Show more folders** to load the next 100. The picker reads at most 10 such pages in one folder.

#### Hidden folders

A hidden folder is a folder with a name that starts with a dot, for example `.git` or `.claude`. The list hides them by default, because they are almost never a good place for a workspace.

1. Look at the button at the right of the **Folder** heading. It reads **Show hidden (3)** when the folder holds three hidden folders.
2. Press it. Expect: the hidden folders appear. The button now reads **Hide hidden**.
3. Press it again to hide them.

The picker remembers the choice in this browser. If a folder holds only hidden folders, the list says "No visible folders" with the count and a **Show hidden** button.

#### Sort and filter

A row above the list has a filter field and a sort menu.

- **Filter folders.** Type three letters or more. The list keeps the folders whose name contains the letters. The case does not matter. With fewer than three letters, the list stays whole. The filter and the sort cover every folder in the list, also the folders that "Show more folders" has not loaded yet. The text "N of M folders" shows while a filter is on, or "N folders match" when every found folder is shown. The cross in the field, or the Escape key, clears the filter. If no folder matches, the list says "No folder matches" and the text you typed. **Up one level** stays.
- **Sort folders.** The default is **Name A–Z**. The names sort in natural order, so `a2` comes before `a10`. You can also choose **Name Z–A**, **Newest first** and **Oldest first**. The two time choices show only when every folder in the list has a modified time.

When you open another folder, the filter clears. The sort choice stays. The picker keeps the sort choice in this browser.

#### The Secrets shortcut

The button **Secrets** is next to the hidden-folder button. It opens the folder of secret files of the Unraid user who runs your terminals. A running session can read the files in this folder. In this folder the picker shows **New secret file**. Type a name (letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, up to 64 characters) and a value, then press **Save secret**. A name without a dot gets the ending `.token`. The new file opens in the file viewer. If the home of the user is not mounted, the picker says so, and you can try again when the array or the session is up.

#### The Favourites strip

The **Favourites** section shows only when you have saved a favourite. It is closed by default and shows "N saved". Press the heading to open it. A card shows the agent icon, the name and the folder. Press a card to fill in the agent and the folder, and then press **Resume** or **Start New**. A card with the mark **Open** belongs to a workspace that is already open. Press it to go to that workspace. A dimmed card is for an agent that is not installed. A pencil and a cross appear on a card when you point at it. The pencil renames the favourite. The cross removes it. See [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md) to learn how to save a favourite.

### Resume or Start New

The footer shows one of two sets of buttons.

| You see | When | What it does |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Only **Start New** | The plugin has no saved conversation for this agent and this folder. | Starts the agent with an empty conversation. |
| **Resume** and **Start New** | The plugin saved a conversation for this agent and this folder when you last closed a workspace there. | **Resume** opens the saved conversation. **Start New** asks first. |

**Start New** with a saved conversation opens the question **Start a new chat?** It says that a saved chat exists. Starting another session does not delete the saved chat, but the agent opens with a blank context. The dialog has three buttons: **Cancel**, **Resume Last** and **Yes, Start New**. Choose **Resume Last** if you pressed the wrong button.

The picker decides which buttons to show when you select an agent or a folder. The buttons can take a moment to change after you select.

### Use the drawer

Each open workspace has one row in the drawer. Select a row to show that workspace in the page. The drawer then closes, unless it is pinned.

**Marks on a row**

| Mark | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| A small green dot on the agent icon | The agent is running. |
| A small grey dot | The agent is stopped. |
| A small orange dot at the top right of the icon | The terminal of this workspace runs an older plugin version than the one installed. See "Move a workspace onto the current version". |
| A speaker with a slash | You turned the voice of this workspace off. |
| An envelope | The workspace keeps its messages as voice mail and does not speak them. |
| A play triangle with a number | Unheard voice mail from this workspace. One press plays the messages, oldest first. |
| A clock | The workspace will continue by itself at a set time. Press the clock to change or cancel the time. |
| The word **upgrading** | An upgrade of this agent is in progress. The row opens when the upgrade ends. |
| The word **storage** | A merge of the home layers is in progress. The row opens when the merge ends. |

Long names. A name that does not fit ends in "...". Point at the row, and the name scrolls once to its end. The tooltip shows the full name. If you set your computer to reduce motion, nothing scrolls and the tooltip shows the name.

Details card. Point at a row for about three quarters of a second. A card opens at the side of the drawer. It shows the status (**Running** or **Stopped**), the path, the agent, the session id, the time of creation, the time of the last activity and the saved conversation, with a small **RESET** button that works like **Restart as new**: it asks first, then starts the workspace again as a new conversation. When the terminal of a workspace is stale, the card also shows two buttons. See "Move a workspace onto the current version".

Order. Drag a row up or down to put it in another place. You can also use **Move up** and **Move down** in the row menu, or press Alt plus the up or down arrow on a row. The page saves the order. A touch screen may not support dragging, so use the row menu there.

Keyboard. Use Tab, Shift plus Tab or the arrow keys to move between rows. Home and End go to the first and the last row. Enter or Space opens the row.

Rename. Select **Rename** in the row menu. The name turns into a text field. Press Enter, or click away, to save. Press Escape to cancel. The plugin does not accept an empty name.

Loading. When you reload the page, the drawer says "Refreshing your workspaces…" until the first list arrives. The text goes away when the list arrives, when there are no workspaces, or when the load fails.

Empty drawer. If no workspace is open and you saved favourites, the drawer shows them under the **New Workspace** button. Press one to open it. It resumes its last conversation if there is one. The drawer shows eight favourites, and a **More…** row opens the picker for the rest.

#### Pin the drawer open

Pinning keeps the drawer open and moves the terminal to the right of it.

1. Open the page on a wide screen.
2. Press the thumbtack on the tab at the left edge. Its title is **Pin drawer open**.
3. Expect: the drawer stays open. The terminal moves to the right so that nothing is hidden. A row of icons appears at the top of the drawer: unpin, temporary terminal, copy the SSH or tmux command, paste, copy, voice and microphone.
4. Press the thumbtack in that row to unpin.

While the drawer is pinned, a click outside it, a click on a row and the Escape key do not close it. The browser remembers the pin. The pin needs a page width of 700 pixels or more, not counting the Unraid side menu. On a narrower page the plugin shows the message "Viewport too narrow to pin the drawer" and does not pin. If the window becomes too narrow while pinned, the plugin unpins the drawer and shows a message.

#### Below the rows

- **Untracked (N).** A session that runs but has no row in your list. Press **Attach** to add it to the list and open it. Press **Close** to stop it. A workspace that you are closing never shows here.
- **Unreachable copies (N).** A second copy of an agent that the terminal cannot reach. Press **Show screen** to read its screen. Press **Stop this copy** to stop it. The visible workspace keeps running.

At the bottom of the drawer there are up to three buttons: the voice mail button (two reels joined by a line, shown when voice mail is available), **Help** and **Settings**.

### The row menu

The menu lists these items, from top to bottom. An item with an arrow at its right is a section. Select the header of a section to open or close it.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Continue** (section): **Continue now**, **Schedule…** | The agent is running. | Types "continue" into the agent now, or at a time that you choose. See [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md). |
| **Switch to** a version, or **Switch to the installed version** | The agent runs a version that differs from the installed version. | Restarts the agent on the installed version and resumes the conversation. See "Move a workspace onto the current version". |
| **Add to favourites** or **Update favourite** | Always. | Saves this agent and this folder as a favourite. The text is **Update favourite** when the favourite exists. |
| **Rename** | Always. | Lets you type another name. |
| **Config / assets** | Always. | Opens the panel for the config, skills and instruction files of this agent. See [Config Hub](config-hub.md). |
| **Details** | Only on a screen that cannot hover, such as a phone. | Opens the details sheet. |
| **Session settings** | Always. | Opens **Manage Session** with the tabs **ENV**, **tmux** and **Args** for this workspace. See [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md). |
| **Voice** (section) | Always. | **Open voice mail**, the choices **Speak**, **Voice mail** and **Off** for this workspace, **Spoken name…** and **Voice…**. See [Voice](voice.md). |
| **Relay** (section): **Inbox**, **Settings** | Always. | The message history of this workspace, and the topics that it listens to. See [Agent Relay](relay.md). |
| **Move** (section): **Move up**, **Move down** | Always. | Changes the place of the row. **Move up** is grey for the first row. **Move down** is grey for the last row. |
| **Upload file** | Always. | Closes the drawer and opens the upload window for the folder of this workspace. See [The terminal](terminal.md). |
| **Export bundle** | Always. | Saves the settings of this workspace in a file. See [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md). |
| **Restart as new** (red) | Always. | Starts the agent again in the same folder without the old conversation. |
| **Close** (red) | Always. | Stops the agent and removes the row. |

Use the arrow keys, Enter and Escape in the menu. On a phone, each item is 44 pixels high. A menu that is taller than the screen scrolls.

### The same workspace on two devices

You can open one workspace in two browsers at once. You can use your desktop and your phone together. Both show the same live terminal. Text that you type in one browser appears in the other. Neither browser knocks the other offline.

1. On the second device, open the AI CLI Agents tab.
2. Select the same row in the drawer.
3. Expect: the terminal shows the same session as on the first device.

Keep these points in mind.

- **Size.** The terminal takes the size of the device you used last. The other device shows the terminal smaller, with empty space around it. You can change this rule per workspace. In **Session settings**, open the **tmux** tab and use the option **Size when shared**. The choices are `latest` (the default), `largest` and `smallest`.
- **Limit.** The plugin keeps up to four browsers on one workspace. When a fifth browser connects, the plugin disconnects the browser that connected first.
- **One conversation.** Both devices type into the same agent. If you type in both at once, the text mixes. Use one device at a time for typing.

### Resume and Restart as new

**Resume** continues a conversation. **Restart as new** starts an empty one. Both keep the workspace itself.

#### How a conversation resumes

When you close a workspace, the plugin reads from the exit screen or from the files of the agent which conversation the workspace was in. It saves that for the pair of agent and folder. **Resume** in the picker opens that conversation. The agents differ in how they name a conversation, and the plugin handles each one.

- **Claude Code** shows the name of a conversation on exit when you named it. The plugin looks for the matching conversation in the project store of the folder and saves its identifier. So **Resume** opens the right conversation and not the picker of Claude Code. If several conversations have the same name and the plugin cannot decide, it keeps the name. Claude Code may then show its own list.
- **Codex CLI** conversations come from the files of Codex. The plugin skips the helper threads that Codex keeps next to your own.
- **OpenCode** resumes the newest conversation of this folder, not the newest conversation of any folder.
- **Codex CLI**, **Kilo Code** and **Goose** continue their newest saved conversation when the agent exits and starts again in the same workspace. The workspace does not open a blank chat at each restart.

The plugin keeps one resume record for each workspace. Two open workspaces with the same agent and the same folder do not take each other's conversation. When the plugin cannot tell which conversation belongs to which workspace, it prefers an empty start to the wrong conversation. For example, after a crash, a workspace that never closed cleanly can open empty. A workspace that you close and open again later on the same folder keeps working as described above.

The setting **Continue after a restart** (Settings, Configuration) is **On** by default. A workspace then continues its work by itself after a restart, an upgrade or a reload that the plugin detects, but never after a plain page load.

#### Restart as new

1. Open the row menu and select **Restart as new**.
2. Expect: the question **Restart as a new conversation?** It names the agent and the folder. It says the plugin closes the agent cleanly, starts it again without resuming, and keeps the old conversation in the history of the agent. It says that Relay peers keep the address of the workspace and learn about the reset on their next contact.
3. Press **Restart as new** to confirm, or **Cancel**.
4. Expect: the page shows "Waking" and the name of the agent. Then the agent shows its first screen.

> [!WARNING]
> The workspace does not open the old conversation again by itself after **Restart as new**. The old conversation stays in the history of the agent, but you must open it from the agent. A later **Close** and **Resume** continues the conversation that the restarted agent made.

The row keeps its name, its place, its settings and its Relay address. The plugin refuses the restart while an upgrade of the agent or a merge of the home layers runs. You then see **Could not restart**, and nothing closes.

**Restart as new** does in one step what you would do with **Close**, the picker and **Start New**.

### Close a workspace

1. Open the row menu and select **Close**.
2. Expect: the row leaves the drawer at once. The plugin then stops the agent. It asks the agent to exit cleanly, reads the conversation identifier from the exit screen, and saves it. This can take several seconds.

The menu item has no confirmation. One case differs. If the workspace is the owner of a Relay topic, the page asks **Pause Relay owner and close?**. If you confirm, the plugin pauses the automatic restart of the owner. The workspace then does not answer requests until you launch it again from **Settings, Agent Relay**.

> [!WARNING]
> **Close** stops the agent. Any work in progress stops. The row, with its name and its place in the list, is removed.

**What is kept**

| Kept | Lost |
| :-- | :-- |
| The conversation, in the history of the agent in your home | The running agent and its terminal |
| The resume record for the agent and the folder, so that **Resume** works | The row, with its name and its place in the drawer |
| The launch arguments, the environment variables and the secrets for the agent and the folder | |
| Your favourites | |
| All the files in the folder of the workspace | |

If you close the last workspace, the page shows **No Active Workspaces** and the button **Select Workspace**.

A workspace that is open when the server restarts comes back by itself after the boot or after the array starts. The plugin also starts it again if the agent exits without warning. A workspace that you closed does not come back.

### Move a workspace onto the current version

A running workspace keeps the version that it started with. This is on purpose, so that an update never interrupts your work. Two cases need your action.

**A newer plugin version.** The terminal of the workspace runs an older plugin version than the one installed. The row shows an orange dot. The details card shows the text "Running an older plugin version than the one installed". It offers two buttons.

| Button | What it does | What it costs |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Reconnect terminal** | Joins the browser to the running session again and reloads the page. The agent keeps running on the old version. | Nothing. Use it when the terminal is blank or dead. |
| **Reload** | Closes the agent, starts it on the current version and resumes the conversation. It sends one "continue". | The agent stops for a moment. |

On a phone, press and hold a row for about half a second to open the details sheet with the same buttons. After an update, the page also shows "A new version was installed — reconnecting all terminals and reloading in" a number of seconds. Press **Not now** to wait.

**Reload** asks first with **Reload onto the current version?**. The dialog says that the plugin closes the agent, starts it again, resumes the conversation and sends one "continue" prompt. It says that anything you typed and did not send is lost, and that work in progress stops. The workspace keeps its name, path, settings, order and Relay address.

> [!WARNING]
> **Reload** and **Switch to** close the running agent. Anything you typed and did not send is lost, and work in progress stops.

The plugin refuses to reload when the agent is busy or in the middle of a prompt. You see **Could not reload**. Try again when the agent is idle. The plugin also refuses when no saved conversation exists, so that you never lose one, and while an upgrade of the agent waits in the Activity tray.

**A different agent version.** You can install another version of an agent while a workspace runs. The workspace keeps the old version. The row menu then shows **Switch to** and the version number. The dialog **Switch to** the version asks for a confirmation with **Switch**. It resumes the conversation. It does not send a "continue", so type your next instruction yourself. The page shows "Now on the installed version" when it ends.

### On a phone

The layout changes when the page is 480 pixels wide or less.

- **The tab at the left edge is short.** It shows three parts: open or close the drawer, the microphone and a "more" button (three dots). Press "more" to show pin, temporary terminal, SSH or tmux copy, paste, copy and voice. These parts fold again after five seconds, after you use one, and when the drawer opens. Drag the first part up or down to move the tab. The tab never goes above the Unraid header.
- **Rows are taller.** Each row is 44 pixels high. A name may use two lines and breaks at hyphens and dots. A name does not scroll.
- **No hover card.** Press and hold a row for about half a second to open the details sheet. You can also use **Details** in the row menu. The sheet shows the full name and the full path.
- **Dialogs use the full width.** The buttons are 44 pixels high, and the action buttons stay at the bottom of the dialog.
- **The drawer cannot be pinned** on a page narrower than 700 pixels.
- **The folder picker** uses the full width. Its controls are 44 pixels high.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Starting folder** (Settings, Configuration) | The folder where the picker starts when no other folder applies. | `/mnt/user` | Set it to the folder that holds your projects. |
| **Which path a workspace runs on** (Settings, Configuration) | Decides where the agent really runs. With **Automatic**, a workspace on a share that only uses the cache pool runs on the pool path. Other folders keep the share path. The row and the favourites keep showing the `/mnt/user` path. | **Automatic** | Leave it. The other choice, "Pool path when the share is on one pool only", is an older mode with the same safe rule. |
| **Continue after a restart** (Settings, Configuration) | Lets a workspace continue by itself after a restart, upgrade or reload. | On | Turn it off if you want to type the next instruction yourself. |
| Show hidden folders (the picker, this browser) | Shows or hides the folders that start with a dot. | Hidden | Turn on to pick a folder such as `.config`. |
| Sort folders (the picker, this browser) | The order of the folder list. | **Name A–Z** | Use the time choices to find a folder you changed lately. |
| Favourites open (the picker, this browser) | Opens or closes the **Favourites** section. | Closed | Open it if you use favourites often. |
| Pin drawer (the drawer, this browser) | Keeps the drawer open beside the terminal. | Off | Pin it on a wide screen if you switch workspaces often. |
| **Size when shared** (Session settings, tmux tab) | Decides which device sets the terminal size when two devices show one workspace. | `latest` | Use `smallest` if you want everything to fit on both devices. |

The workspace working directory rule has one effect to know. Claude Code and OpenCode keep the history of a conversation for each folder. A workspace that opens again on another launch path may start a separate history.

## What happens behind the scenes

Each workspace runs in a tmux session (the session manager that keeps a terminal alive on the server). The browser terminal attaches to it. Several browsers can attach to one session. The plugin keeps the list of workspaces, the order, the names and the resume records in your home, and it saves them with the rest of the home. See C4 Component: Session Process Management for the lifecycle of a workspace and C4 Component: React Terminal Spa for the drawer and the picker.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The drawer is empty after a reload | The page is still loading the list. | Wait for "Refreshing your workspaces…" to go away. |
| **No Active Workspaces** | No workspace is open. | Press **Select Workspace**. |
| The picker has no **Resume** button | The plugin has no saved conversation for this agent and this folder. | Press **Start New**. A conversation saves when a workspace closes cleanly. |
| An agent opens with an empty conversation after **Resume** | Two workspaces share the folder and the agent, or the plugin could not find the conversation. | Open the conversation from the agent itself. |
| Claude Code shows its own list of sessions | Several conversations have the same name. | Choose the right one in the list. Give the conversations different names. |
| A row under **Untracked** | An agent runs that has no row in your list. | Press **Attach** to use it, or **Close** to stop it. |
| A row under **Unreachable copies** | A second copy of an agent runs and the terminal cannot reach it. | Press **Show screen** to see it. Press **Stop this copy** to stop it. |
| A row with **upgrading** or **storage** | The agent upgrades, or the plugin merges the home layers. | Wait. The row opens again by itself. |
| A blank or white terminal after an update | The terminal bridge runs the old plugin version. | Use **Reconnect terminal** in the details card. |
| **Could not reload**, **Could not restart** or **Could not continue** | The agent is busy, an upgrade runs, or no saved conversation exists. | Read the message, wait until the agent is idle, and try again. |
| **Could not start this workspace** or **Could not close this workspace** | The server refused the request or did not answer. A failed close keeps the workspace row. | Read the message. Check the **Debug Console** for the reason, then try again when the agent is ready. |
| **Storage Unavailable** after a reboot | The folder of the workspace is not mounted yet. | Wait. The page tries again every 10 seconds. |
| **Workspace Folder Missing** | The storage is mounted, but the folder of the workspace was deleted or moved. The card shows the folder path. | Waiting does not help. Close the workspace, or choose another folder for it. Open another workspace in the drawer: the card goes away. |
| "Viewport too narrow to pin the drawer" | The page is less than 700 pixels wide. | Make the window wider, or use the drawer without the pin. |
| The terminal looks small on your desktop | A phone or a tablet is attached to the same workspace. | Close it on the other device, or set **Size when shared** to `largest`. |
| **Could not create folder** | The server refused to create the folder. | Read the message in the dialog. Choose another name or folder. |
| **Could not read this folder** in the picker | The server could not list the folder. | Read the reason. Choose another folder. |
| **Could not stop** after **Close** on an untracked row | The server refused to stop the session, or the request failed. The row stays. | Read the message and press **Close** again. |
| A red message at the top of **Manage Session** | The plugin could not read the settings of this workspace. Saving is off, so a save cannot erase them. | Close the dialog and open it again. |

For other problems, see [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md).

- **2026-10-22** — The settings have new labels: **Starting folder** and **Which path a workspace runs on**. Spec `docs/specs/SETTINGS_PAGE_FIRST_CLASS_REDESIGN.md`, issue #750.
- **2026-10-18** — A failed start shows the server reason, and a failed close keeps the workspace row and shows an error. Spec `docs/specs/WORKSPACE_SERVER_AUTHORITY.md`, issue #671.
- **2026-10-18** — The picker says why a folder could not be read, **Close** on an untracked row keeps the row and says why when the stop fails, and **Manage Session** shows a red message and turns saving off when it cannot read the settings. Issue #670.
